Post-conviction, he was taken into custody, and after suffering imprisonment for almost two months, bail was granted by this Court in CRL.A. No. 95/2014.

4. Despite the aforesaid criminal background post-conviction, it appears that respondent no.3 not only continued the employment of respondent no.4 but post his superannuation, again took his services on contract basis, which has prompted petitioner to refer this petition seeking certain reliefs Manish Kumar Gupta vs Govt Of Nct Of Delhi & Ors on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53785295/
1 against respondent no.1 & 2 and also action against respondent no.3.

sentences.text:
It is brought on record that respondent no.3 has adopted the Central Civil Services (Conduct)
Rules, 1964 ('CCS Rules') qua the conduct of its employees by a Resolution, and pursuant to the CCS Rules, it is claimed by petitioner that the services of respondent no.4 ought not to have been continued or thereafter taken on contract basis.
To substantiate such contentions, the provisions of the CCS Rules are sought to be relied on.
6. As against above, counsel for respondent no.4-employee claims that he has superannuated and post-conviction, he was demoted.
Today he remains untouched with the business of respondent no.3/Society and as such the petition can be termed as infructuous and be accordingly disposed of.

7. This apart, contentions of respondent nos.3 & 4 are that respondent no.3, a Credit Co-operative Society, even though registered under the Delhi Co-operative Societies Act, 2003, cannot be termed as 'State' within the meaning of Article 12 of the Constitution of India, 1950, and for the relief claimed in the writ petition is not maintainable as against a private body.

8. Reliance is placed by respondents on the judgment of Single Judge of this Court in W.P.(C)
7462/2022 titled as "Sunita Sharma & Ors. vs. Delhi State Co-operative Bank Ltd. & Anr."

As against above, counsel for petitioner has claimed that not only the writ petition is maintainable against respondent no.3/Credit Co-operative Society, but also against respondent nos.1 & 2,
particularly when respondent no.3 is a body registered, pursuant to the provisions of Delhi Co-operative Societies Act, 2003.
10. Written submissions of petitioner are on record.
However, he seeks time to place on record judgments in support of aforesaid contentions.
11. Similarly, counsel for respondent nos.3 & 4 seeks time to place on record written submissions.

12. List on 18th September 2025.
13.
